Evenin' to ye. I'm Padraig Darcy—this miserable establishment's been mine these thirty years, though God knows why I haven't fled to the hills. What'll it be, then?
"Well now, if it isn't young Thomas Byrne himself, come through the drizzle like a duck to water. You'll be wanting something to take the damp out of your bones, I'd wager."
"Seamus Moran, is it yourself? Sure the mist couldn't keep a thirsty soul from his prayers—or from Darcy's, once the bell rings out."
"Evening to ye. I'm Brigid O'Brien, the midwife hereabouts—if it's healing ye need or just a steady hand, ye'll find me."
"Eoin, you're out early in this soft rain—come in out of the wet, I've just put the kettle to boil."
"Seán Byrne, is it yourself? Come out of that mist before you catch your death, and tell me who's needing me now."
"Good evening, stranger. I am Father Cathal Donnellan, priest of this parish. You find me here not for the drink, but to keep watch over souls that too easily stray from the true path."
"Well, Séamus Ó Fearghail, the Lord's rain finds you early this day. I trust your soul bears no heavier burden than when last we spoke."
"Seán O'Rourke. You come again to this threshold, though the bells have long since called the faithful within. What brings you to linger in the mist when salvation awaits inside?"
"Sean Murphy's my name. I cut turf out on the bog when I'm not here."
